rule_level_problems.problem: The duration uses >= 4 weeks where the page says > 4 weeks, and 'most days' (persistent symptoms) is lost. With onset at least 4 weeks ago plus a Recurrent qualifier, the rule fires on any recurrent nasal symptom that first began 4+ weeks ago, even if it occurs rarely.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable sinusitis from nose symptoms
rule_level_problems.problem: 'Headache worse on bending forward' is reduced to plain Headache, a common symptom, so the discriminating feature is lost. The rule also strictly ANDs tenderness, headache and a recent common cold. Separately, 'recent common cold' is a Recent-qualified clinical_finding, so a Common cold diagnosed earlier by this page's own rule (a diagnosis/active_condition) will not satisfy it.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable common cold / acute viral infection from nose symptoms
rule_level_problems.problem: 'Less than 3 days' is encoded with <= (inclusive), but the briefing's convention for 'within' is <. Fever is also represented inconsistently: onset of (active_condition Fever) here, but the Mild-qualified clinical_finding Fever in the diphtheria rule and check_for. The common cold No branch requires a recorded temperature below 38 °C.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose possible diphtheria from nose symptoms
rule_level_problems.problem: It uses (clinical_finding Fever + Mild) rather than (active_condition Fever), so fever recorded as a common symptom will not satisfy it unless it was entered with the Mild qualifier through the check_for.

summary: The red box (head injury with clear watery nasal discharge, Urgent) and every 'likely' and 'consider' conclusion on the page are encoded with valid SNOMED concepts and the right rule types. The most consequential gaps are two. In the allergic rhinitis rule, the duration boundary is wrong (>= 4 weeks instead of > 4 weeks) and 'most days' is lost. In the sinusitis rule, 'headache worse on bending forward' is reduced to plain Headache. The '< 3 days' criterion also uses an inclusive <=.
